mainTopic: Unwitting עבודה זרה: רבא's view on worship out of love or fear, and whether several acts of עבודה זרה done in one העלם need one חטאת or many.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רבא, who holds that worshipping an idol out of love or fear of a person is פטור. He answers that the unwitting case in the ברייתא is a כהן who thinks idol worship is entirely permitted, which is different from העלם דבר. Next, רבי זכאי teaches that someone who did four kinds of עבודה זרה in one העלם brings only one חטאת. רבי יוחנן rejects this: 'Go teach it outside.' רבי אבא ties רבי זכאי's view to רבי יוסי, who says הבערה on שבת was singled out only to make it a plain לאו, not to divide the מלאכות. רב יוסף objects that רבי יוסי already learns the dividing of שבת labors from 'ועשה מאחת מהנה', so for עבודה זרה he might agree that השתחוואה comes to divide. The גמרא tries to apply that same פסוק to עבודה זרה. It works out a case of unknowing עבודה זרה, but then shows the פסוק belongs to ויקרא chapter 4, which cannot be about עבודה זרה, and the attempt is dropped. The amud ends as רב שמואל בר יהודה arrives with a new teaching.

steps.title: The only remaining case is bowing out of love or fear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge against רבא. Since bowing to a statue of a person without accepting him as a god is meaningless, the ברייתא's unwitting case must be bowing out of love or fear. That would show such bowing counts as עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he did not accept the person as a god, his bowing means nothing. So doesn't the ברייתא have to be talking about someone who bowed out of love or out of fear?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out the last possible case and lands on 'love or fear' as the only way to explain the ברייתא. This is a direct challenge to רבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a כהן משיח can bring a קרבן for unwitting עבודה זרה, so a real case of שגגה must exist. Bowing to a person's statue is either מזיד (if he accepted it as a god) or nothing at all (if he didn't). That leaves love or fear as the only real שגגה, which would mean it is considered עבודה זרה, against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted it upon himself as a god
It is nothing; it has no legal weight
Rather, isn't it…? (introduces the only remaining option, used as a proof)
Out of love or out of fear of a person

steps.confusionAlert: 'Love or fear' here does not mean love or fear of the idol. It means he bowed because he loved or feared a person, for example a king, without believing in the idol at all.

phrases.english: And if he did not accept him upon himself as a god –
phrases.notes: This is still talking about bowing to a statue of a person, the case the גמרא brought up just before this.

phrases.english: it is nothing.
Rather, is it not a case of love or fear?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, מֵאַהֲבָה וּמִיִּרְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the elimination argument begun before this section, which tested each possible case of an unwitting כהן משיח.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's position that worshipping out of love or fear is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every other case of 'unwitting' עבודה זרה is either intentional or not worship at all. Only love or fear fits the ברייתא, so love or fear must count as worship.

steps.title: רבא: the case is one who thinks idol worship is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for רבא with another case of שגגה: the כהן knows he is worshipping an idol but mistakenly thinks this is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא can answer you: No. The ברייתא is talking about someone who says idol worship is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבא by finding a different case of unwitting idol worship, so 'love or fear' is no longer forced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that worshipping out of love or fear was the only possible unwitting case. רבא points to a different mistake about the law: the כהן truly serves the idol but wrongly believes idol worship is permitted. That counts as שגגה without needing love or fear.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (introduces a possible answer for that אמורא)
In a case where he says it is permitted

phrases.english: And Rava could say to you:
No, it is a case where he says it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case of the ברייתא (finding another possible case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only love or fear could be the unwitting case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא can be talking about a כהן who serves the idol while mistakenly believing it is permitted.

steps.title: But thinking it is permitted is just העלם דבר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a person who thinks idol worship is permitted is exactly the case of העלם דבר. In that case רבי and חכמים agree, so the ברייתא's argument would have nothing left to argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says it is permitted, that is the same as העלם דבר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer, saying his case is already a known category and cannot be the subject of the dispute in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי and חכמים argue about the כהן משיח's קרבן, but in a case of העלם דבר (forgetting the law) even חכמים agree he brings one. If רבא's case is simply העלם דבר, the ברייתא's argument loses its meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as
A mistake about the law itself (literally, 'the matter was hidden')

phrases.english: Says it is permitted –
that is the same as a lapse of awareness of the law!
phrases.notes: In that case the חכמים agree with רבי that the כהן משיח brings a קרבן, so there would be no argument left.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמֵר מוּתָּר, הַיְינוּ הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given for רבא in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's case of 'he says it is permitted'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case is identical to העלם דבר, where both sides of the ברייתא agree. It therefore cannot explain a case they argue about.

steps.title: Entirely permitted versus partly permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא separates the two cases. רבא's case is a כהן who thinks idol worship is completely permitted. העלם דבר is a כהן who keeps part of the איסור but wrongly cancels another part.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he says it is entirely permitted. העלם דבר means keeping part of the איסור and cancelling part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by showing that his case is different from העלם דבר. The ברייתא's argument stays meaningful, and רבא's view survives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: העלם דבר is a partial mistake: the person knows idol worship is forbidden but thinks some forms of it are allowed. רבא's case is a total mistake, where he thinks all idol worship is permitted. רבי and חכמים can argue about the total mistake, so the ברייתא never forces 'love or fear', and רבא is not refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: Entirely, completely
Upholding part of the איסור
Cancelling part of the איסור

steps.whatToRemember: העלם דבר requires a partial mistake: keeping part of the איסור and cancelling part. Thinking an איסור is entirely permitted is a different category, and with this distinction רבא's view, that bowing out of love or fear is exempt, stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that העלם דבר means 'קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת' is a basic principle about קרבנות for mistaken rulings, discussed at length in מסכת הוריות.

phrases.english: It is where he says it is entirely permitted.
A lapse of awareness of the law –
is upholding part and cancelling part.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוֹמֵר מוּתָּר לִגְמָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by refining the case given in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between two similar cases (a total versus a partial mistake about the law)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any belief that idol worship is permitted is העלם דבר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a partial mistake (קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת) is העלם דבר. Thinking it is entirely permitted is a separate case, and that is the case רבי and חכמים argue about.

steps.title: רבי זכאי's teaching: several acts of idol worship, one offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכאי teaches a ברייתא in front of רבי יוחנן. If someone did four different acts of עבודה זרה in one העלם, he brings only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זכאי taught in front of רבי יוחנן: If someone sacrificed, burned incense, poured a libation and bowed to an idol, all while forgetting once, he owes only one offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי זכאי quotes a ברייתא about how many חטאת offerings a person owes for doing several kinds of idol worship by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four acts are four different ways of serving an idol. The ברייתא treats them as one big sin, so the person brings one חטאת. This is the claim the next steps will react to.

keyTerms.meaning: He slaughtered an animal as an offering (here, to an idol)
He burned incense or offering parts on the altar
He poured a libation (a drink offering)
He bowed down
One lapse of awareness: he forgot the איסור once and did everything during that single forgetting

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think he is exempt for some of the acts. The question is only how many חטאת offerings he brings: one for all of them, or one for each act.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַבִּי זַכַּאי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zakkai taught before Rabbi Yoḥanan:
If one sacrificed, and burned incense, and poured a libation, and bowed down to an idol
all in one lapse of awareness
he is obligated to bring only one sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי זַכַּאי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the רבא discussion in steps 1-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Several different acts of עבודה זרה done in one העלם require only one חטאת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rejects the teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells רבי זכאי to go teach that ברייתא outside. In other words, it does not belong in the בית מדרש because it is not the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Go out and teach it outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן strongly rejects רבי זכאי's ברייתא. He holds that each act of idol worship gets its own offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "teach it outside" means this ruling should not be taught as accepted הלכה. So רבי יוחנן holds a person brings a separate חטאת for each kind of עבודה זרה. This sets up the question of where רבי זכאי's view came from.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out
Teach it outside, meaning not in the study hall, because it is not accepted

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him:
Go out and teach it outside.
phrases.notes: A sharp way of saying: this teaching is wrong, so don't teach it here in the בית מדרש.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹק תְּנִי לְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the ברייתא taught in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole ruling that only one חטאת is brought for several acts of עבודה זרה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against the accepted הלכה that each act of עבודה זרה requires its own חטאת.

steps.title: רבי אבא links רבי זכאי's view to a dispute about kindling on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says רבי זכאי's teaching is really one side of a מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and רבי נתן. They argue about why the תורה singled out הבערה from the other שבת labors. רבי יוסי says it was to make it a plain לאו. רבי נתן says it was to teach that each מלאכה counts separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: What רבי זכאי said depends on a מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and רבי נתן. A ברייתא teaches: Kindling was singled out to make it a plain prohibition, says רבי יוסי. רבי נתן says: it was singled out to divide.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא defends רבי זכאי. He shows that his ruling is not baseless and fits one side of an older מחלוקת between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה separately says not to kindle fire on שבת (שמות 35:3). רבי נתן learns from this that each מלאכה is its own sin, so you owe a separate חטאת for each one. רבי יוסי uses the verse for something else, a plain לאו. So he has no source for splitting the acts, and רבי זכאי's "only one" fits his view. The גמרא will work out how this carries over to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Kindling a fire, one of the 39 מלאכות of שבת
It was singled out to make it a plain prohibition, without the death penalty other מלאכות carry
It was singled out to divide: to teach that each מלאכה is a separate sin
A dispute between Sages

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זכאי's ruling (one חטאת for many acts of idol worship) is tied to רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי uses the separate mention of הבערה as a plain לאו, not as a lesson to divide. רבי נתן uses it "לחלק", which leads to a separate חטאת for each act.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי and רבי נתן are not arguing about whether kindling on שבת is forbidden. Both agree it is. They argue only about what the Torah wanted to teach by mentioning it separately.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of "לחלק" is a key tool across ש״ס. It explains why someone can owe many חטאת offerings in one forgetting when the acts are separate categories.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba says:
That which Rabbi Zakkai says
is the subject of a dispute between Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Natan,
as it is taught in a baraita:
Kindling was singled out to make it an ordinary prohibition,
phrases.notes: Kindling is singled out in שמות 35:3. Here it means kindling is only a לאו, not punished by stoning like other מלאכות.

phrases.english: this is the statement of Rabbi Yosei.
And Rabbi Natan says:
It was singled out to divide.
phrases.notes: He means each מלאכה on שבת counts on its own, so each one needs its own חטאת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זַכַּאי מַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's rejection by showing that רבי זכאי's ruling follows רבי יוסי's side of an older מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זכאי's teaching depends on the מחלוקת of רבי יוסי (הבערה singled out ללאו) and רבי נתן (הבערה singled out לחלק).

steps.title: Bowing works like kindling
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא compares השתחוואה to הבערה. Each תנא who explains why הבערה was singled out would explain השתחוואה the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you hold that kindling was singled out to make it a plain prohibition, then bowing was also singled out to make it a plain prohibition. If you hold that kindling was singled out to divide, then bowing was also singled out to divide.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא finishes his explanation from the last step. He applies the רבי יוסי / רבי נתן argument about הבערה to השתחוואה in עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists השתחוואה on its own, apart from the other kinds of serving an idol. For רבי יוסי, that only makes it a plain לאו, so the acts are not counted one by one, and one העלם brings one חטאת. That fits רבי זכאי's ברייתא. For רבי נתן, singling it out teaches that each kind of עבודה זרה counts separately.

keyTerms.meaning: Kindling a fire on שבת
Bowing down to an idol
Was singled out to make it a plain prohibition
Was singled out to divide, so each act counts on its own

steps.whyThisMatters: This links רבי זכאי's ברייתא to a known תנא. So רבי יוחנן's rejection of it means the הלכה does not follow that side.

phrases.english: According to the one who says kindling was singled out to be a plain prohibition,
bowing was also singled out to be a plain prohibition.
According to the one who says kindling was singled out to divide,
bowing was also singled out to divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הַבְעָרָה לְלָאו יָצָאת, הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה נָמֵי לְלָאו יָצָאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי אבא's explanation by applying the הבערה argument to השתחוואה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each תנא reads השתחוואה the way he reads הבערה. So רבי זכאי's one-חטאת ברייתא follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוסי divides from a different verse
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רבי אבא. רבי יוסי may call הבערה a plain לאו only because he has a different source for dividing the שבת labors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: Maybe רבי יוסי only said there that kindling was singled out as a plain prohibition because he learns the division of labors from the words 'one of them'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף questions the comparison. He says רבי יוסי's view on הבערה may not carry over to השתחוואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שבת, רבי יוסי already has 'אחת מהנה' to teach that each מלאכה counts separately. So he did not need הבערה for that job, and he used it for a plain לאו. For עבודה זרה he may have no such other source. If so, he might read השתחוואה as coming to divide, and רבי זכאי's ברייתא would not clearly follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it
Perhaps
Counting each מלאכה separately, a חטאת for each
'One of them', from the פסוק about bringing a חטאת

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects to this:

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Yosei only said
there, that kindling was singled out to be a plain prohibition,
because he derives the division of labors
from 'one of them'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אבא's comparison of השתחוואה to הבערה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's claim that רבי יוסי would read השתחוואה as a plain לאו, just like הבערה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's reading of הבערה depends on his having another source for dividing שבת labors. That reason may not apply to עבודה זרה, so the comparison may fail.

steps.title: רבי יוסי learns from 'one of them'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי does learn from 'ועשה מאחת מהנה'. Sometimes there is one חטאת for everything, and sometimes a חטאת for each act.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יוסי says, 'and does from one of them.' Sometimes a person owes one offering for all of them, and sometimes he owes one for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב יוסף. It shows that רבי יוסי really does take division of sins from the words 'אחת מהנה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי reads the פסוק's words as pointing both ways. Sometimes it is 'אחת', one חטאת for everything, and sometimes it is 'מהנה', one for each. So he has his own source for counting שבת labors separately. That supports רב יוסף's point that he did not need הבערה for this.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
Each and every one

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says,
'and does from one of them'
sometimes he is liable one offering for all of them,

phrases.aramaic: פְּעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.
phrases.english: sometimes he is liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, וְעָשָׂה מֵאַחַת מֵהֵנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב יוסף's claim that רבי יוסי learns division of labors from 'אחת מהנה'.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that רבי יוסי has a separate source for dividing שבת labors.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יוסי explains 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' as meaning sometimes one חטאת for all, and sometimes one for each.

steps.title: רבי יונתן explains רבי יוסי's source
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן shows that רבי יוסי learns from the extra letters of 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' that one act can count as many, and many acts can count as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said: What is רבי יוסי's reason? The פסוק says 'And does from one of them.' It could have said 'one' but says 'from one.' It could have said 'them' but says 'of them.' This teaches that sometimes one act counts as many, and sometimes many acts count as one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly how רבי יוסי reads the פסוק from the ברייתא in the last step. This is the source he uses for dividing the שבת labors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra letter מ in 'מאחת' and 'מהנה' is the key to the דרשה. From it רבי יוסי learns two opposite cases: one act that gets many חטאות, and many acts that get only one חטאת. This proves רבי יוסי has his own source for dividing the labors, which is exactly what רב יוסף needs for his challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason (the source) for this opinion?
'And does from one of them': the פסוק about bringing a חטאת
One act that counts as many
Many acts that count as one

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yonatan said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?
As it is written: "And does from one of them."
"One" is written as "from one."
"Them" is written as "of them."
One that is many,
and many that is one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the exact פסוק reading behind the ruling of רבי יוסי quoted in the ברייתא of step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי learns from the extra letters of 'מאחת מהנה' that there are cases of one act that counts as many, and many acts that count as one.

steps.title: Partial acts and offshoot labors are included
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains what each word of the פסוק adds: writing part of a word still counts, and the תולדות count along with the אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One' means writing a full word like שמעון. 'From one' means writing just part of it, like the letters שם out of שמעון, which still makes you liable. 'Them' means the main labors (אבות). 'Of them' adds the offshoot labors (תולדות).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן goes word by word through the פסוק and shows what each one teaches about the laws of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra מ in 'מאחת' teaches that even part of a planned act is enough for a חטאת. Writing שם counts even though he meant to write שמעון, because שם is a word on its own. The extra מ in 'מהנה' brings in the תולדות, so they also obligate a חטאת just like the אבות.

keyTerms.meaning: The letters שם taken from the name שמעון, a partial act that still counts as writing
The main categories of שבת labor
Offshoot labors that come from the main categories

phrases.english: "One" means writing "Shimon,"
"From one" means writing "Shem" out of "Shimon."
phrases.notes: He planned to write the whole name but only wrote the first two letters, which already spell a real word.

phrases.english: "Them" means the main labors,
"Of them" means the offshoot labors.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אַחַת״ – ״שִׁמְעוֹן״, ״מֵאַחַת״ – ״שֵׁם״ מִ״שִּׁמְעוֹן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the details of the פסוק reading from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partial act like writing שם from שמעון obligates a חטאת, and the תולדות are included along with the אבות.

steps.title: When one act counts as many, and many as one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן defines the two cases. Knowing it is שבת but not knowing the labors are forbidden means a חטאת for each labor. Forgetting it is שבת but knowing the labors are forbidden means only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One that is many' is when a person knows it is שבת but does not know these labors are forbidden. He brings a חטאת for each labor. 'Many that is one' is when he forgets it is שבת but knows the labors are forbidden. He brings only one חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן explains which real-life cases fit 'one that is many' and 'many that is one.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is what the person forgot. If he forgot the laws of each מלאכה, each mistake is a separate error, so he brings a separate חטאת for each. If he forgot only that it was שבת, it is all one mistake, so he brings one חטאת for everything. This is the 'dividing of labors' that רבי יוסי learns from this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowing that today is שבת
Not knowing that these labors are forbidden
Forgetting that today is שבת
Knowing that these labors are forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Knowing it is שבת leads to MANY חטאות, because each forgotten law is its own mistake. Forgetting it is שבת leads to only ONE חטאת, because there was only one mistake.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי already has a פסוק ('ועשה מאחת מהנה') that teaches the dividing of שבת labors. So he does not need הבערה for that.

phrases.english: "One" that is "many":
knowing it is Shabbat, but not knowing the labors are forbidden.
"Many" that is "one":
forgetting it is Shabbat, but knowing the labors are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אַחַת״ שֶׁהִיא ״הֵנָּה״: זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יונתן's explanation by defining the two cases learned in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Knowing it is שבת but not knowing the labors are forbidden means a חטאת for each labor. Forgetting it is שבת but knowing the labors are forbidden means one חטאת.

steps.title: With idol worship, everyone may agree bowing was singled out to divide
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף finishes his challenge. With עבודה זרה there is no other source for dividing the acts, so even רבי יוסי may agree that השתחוואה was singled out to divide.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, with עבודה זרה, there is no other place to learn the dividing of acts. So everyone may agree that bowing was singled out to teach that each act counts separately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב יוסף's challenge to its punchline. The comparison between השתחוואה and הבערה does not hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי could say הבערה was singled out only as a plain לאו, because he already learned the dividing of שבת labors from 'מאחת מהנה.' With עבודה זרה there is no such פסוק. So השתחוואה may be needed to teach dividing, and then even רבי יוסי would agree. This breaks רבי אבא's claim that the two cases match תנא for תנא. It also undercuts his attempt to tie רבי זכאי's teaching to the מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: Dividing the acts, so that each one counts as a separate sin
From another place (another source)
Everyone agrees
It was singled out to divide

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a tanna's reading of one case (הבערה) may depend on what other sources he has. So you cannot simply copy his view to a different case (השתחוואה).
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's point: רבי יוסי's view on הבערה depends on his extra source for שבת. Since עבודה זרה has no such source, השתחוואה may teach dividing according to everyone.

phrases.english: But here,
where he does not derive the dividing of the acts
from another place,
everyone agrees
that bowing was singled out to divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּלָא נָפְקָא לֵיהּ חִילּוּק מְלָאכוֹת מִדּוּכְתָּא אַחֲרִיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the proof from steps 10–13, that רבי יוסי has a separate source for שבת, to finish the challenge opened in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's comparison (step 8) that each תנא explains השתחוואה the same way he explains הבערה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's view of הבערה as a plain לאו relies on his having another source ('מאחת מהנה') for dividing שבת labors. עבודה זרה has no such source, so השתחוואה may be needed to teach dividing according to everyone, and the comparison fails.

steps.title: Why not learn the division of idol-worship acts from 'one of them'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the division of acts of עבודה זרה cannot come from 'ועשה מאחת מהנה'. It shows how each word of the פסוק would apply: full acts, partial acts, main categories, and sub-categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not also learn the division of acts of idol worship from 'one of them'? 'One' means a full sacrifice. 'From one' means cutting only one of the two neck organs. 'Them' means the main types: sacrificing, burning incense, pouring wine, and bowing. 'Of them' means the sub-types, like breaking a stick in front of an idol.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that השתחוואה had to be singled out to divide the acts of עבודה זרה. It suggests the same פסוק that divides the labors of שבת could do this job too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, רב יוסף said that for עבודה זרה there is no other source for dividing acts, so השתחוואה must be the source. Here the גמרא points out that 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' is a general פסוק, not limited to שבת. So רבי יונתן's reading of each word in step 12 could be copied over to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Dividing the acts, so that each act brings its own קרבן
Slaughtering an animal as an offering
One of the two organs cut in שחיטה: the windpipe or the food pipe
Burning incense or offerings
Pouring a drink offering
Breaking a stick, a sub-type of slaughtering

phrases.english: The division of acts of idol worship
let him also derive it from "one of them"?
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק רבי יוסי used for שבת back in step 10 (ויקרא 4:2).

phrases.english: "One" means slaughtering;
"From one" means one organ.
phrases.notes: He cut only one of the two neck organs, so it is a partial act, like writing part of a word on שבת.

phrases.english: "Them" means the main categories:
sacrificing, burning, pouring, and bowing.
"Of them" means the sub-categories:
he broke a stick in front of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִילּוּק מְלָאכוֹת דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נָמֵי תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מֵאַחַת מֵהֵנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's claim in step 14 that עבודה זרה has no other source for dividing acts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that השתחוואה must be the source for dividing the acts of עבודה זרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' is general, so its word-by-word reading could apply to עבודה זרה just as it does to שבת.

steps.title: The two cases of the פסוק applied to idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The challenge continues by applying the two cases from step 13 to עבודה זרה. In one case, a single sin counts as many. In the other, many sins count as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One' that is 'many': he knew idol worship is forbidden but did not know these acts are forbidden. 'Many' that is 'one': he did not know about idol worship but knew these acts are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its suggestion. It shows that רבי יונתן's two cases from שבת also fit עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שבת, knowing it is שבת but not knowing the labors are forbidden means a חטאת for each act. Forgetting שבת means only one חטאת. Here the גמרא swaps in עבודה זרה. Knowing about עבודה זרה but not knowing the acts means many חטאות. Not knowing about עבודה זרה means one.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowing; doing it with awareness that it is forbidden
Not knowing; doing it by mistake
The specific acts of worship

phrases.english: "One" that is "many":
knowing about idol worship, but not knowing about the acts.
"Many" that is "one":
not knowing about idol worship, but knowing about the acts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַת שֶׁהִיא הֵנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 15 by applying the cases of step 13 to עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that השתחוואה must be the source for dividing the acts of עבודה זרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every part of רבי יונתן's reading, including the two cases, seems to fit עבודה זרה, so the פסוק could be the source.

steps.title: What could 'not knowing about idol worship' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion by asking what case could count as not knowing about עבודה זרה. If he thought the building was a בית הכנסת, his heart was toward Heaven, so that case does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case of not knowing about idol worship, what does it look like? If he thought it was a synagogue and bowed to it, his heart was toward Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion by testing whether a case of 'not knowing about עבודה זרה' can really exist. This opens a search for such a case that runs through the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of 'many that are one' needs someone who did not know about עבודה זרה. The first possible case fails. A man who thought he was bowing at a בית הכנסת was serving Heaven, so he did not sin at all and brings no קרבן. The גמרא will go on to test other possible cases.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it look like? What is the case?
A synagogue
His heart was directed toward Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a case of a mistaken sin that needs a חטאת. Because his heart was toward Heaven, he did no עבודה זרה at all.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי שִׁגְגַת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, הֵיכִי דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: This case of not knowing about idol worship, what is it like?
If he thought it was a synagogue
and bowed to it,
then his heart was toward Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי שִׁגְגַת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 16's case of 'many that are one' by asking whether a real case of not knowing about עבודה זרה can exist. Steps 19 and 21 answer it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case of 'many that are one' (שגגת עבודה זרה וזדון עבודות) as applied to עבודה זרה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The first possible case, mistaking an idol house for a בית הכנסת, is no sin at all, since his heart was toward Heaven.

steps.title: The statue case does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a man who bowed to a statue of a person. Either he accepted it as a god, which makes him a מזיד, or he did not, which means he did nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe it is where he saw a statue of a person and bowed to it. But if he accepted it as a god, he did it on purpose. If he did not accept it as a god, what he did is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second case of unknowing עבודה זרה, a man bowing to a statue, and shows right away that it fails too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is only brought for a sin done without knowing. If the man accepted the statue as a god, he knew what he was doing, so he is a מזיד. If he only bowed to honor the person, that is not עבודה זרה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A statue, usually of a king or other person
He accepted it upon himself as a god
One who sins on purpose. He gets punished and does not bring a קרבן.
Nothing. No sin at all.

phrases.english: Rather, where he saw a statue
phrases.notes: This is a statue of a person, like a king, not a known idol.

phrases.english: and bowed to it.
If he accepted it upon himself as a god, he is acting on purpose;

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא קַבְּלֵיהּ עֲלֵיהּ – לָא כְּלוּם הוּא.
phrases.english: if he did not accept it upon himself, it is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דַּחֲזָא אִנְדְּרָטָא וּסְגֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 17's search for a case of unknowing עבודה זרה after the בית הכנסת case failed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the statue case as an example of unknowing עבודה זרה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Either he knew he was serving it as a god, so he is a מזיד, or he did not serve it as a god at all.

steps.title: Worshipping out of love or fear
steps.stepSummary: A new case is offered. He served an idol out of love or fear of a person and did not know this is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where he worshipped out of love or out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a case that seems to work. Someone worshipped an idol because he loved or feared a person, and did not know this was forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here he does not accept the idol as a god, but he still does an act of worship. If that counts as עבודה זרה, then not knowing it is forbidden would make it a sin done without knowing, which needs a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Out of love for a person, not belief in the idol
Out of fear of a person

phrases.english: Rather, it is out of love or out of fear.
phrases.notes: He served the idol to please or to protect himself from a person, without believing in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵאַהֲבָה וּמִיִּרְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed statue case with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No real case of unknowing עבודה זרה can be found.
steps.terutzMaskana: Worship out of love or fear, without knowing it is forbidden, could be such a case.

steps.title: That only works for אביי, not רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that one who worships out of love or fear is חייב, so the case works for him. רבא holds he is פטור, so for רבא the case fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for אביי, who says he is liable. But according to רבא, who says he is exempt, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the love-or-fear case. Only one of two אמוראים would accept it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא argue whether worship out of love or fear counts as עבודה זרה. For רבא it is not a sin even on purpose, so it cannot be a case that needs a חטאת. We still need a case that works for רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well, but only for one opinion
Liable
Exempt
What can be said? A way of asking how the other opinion would explain it.

phrases.english: This works well for אביי, who says he is liable;
but according to רבא, who says he is exempt,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְאַבַּיֵּי, דְּאָמַר חַיָּיב; אֶלָּא לְרָבָא, דְּאָמַר פָּטוּר, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the love-or-fear case from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The love-or-fear case as the example of unknowing עבודה זרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא holds that worship out of love or fear is פטור even on purpose, so it cannot be a sin done without knowing that needs a חטאת.

steps.title: He thinks עבודה זרה is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The case that works for רבא is someone who thinks עבודה זרה is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where he says, 'It is permitted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a case that works for everyone. The person knows he is serving an idol but thinks it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He really does serve the idol, so it is עבודה זרה even for רבא. He does not know it is forbidden, so it is a sin done without knowing. That makes it a proper case for a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: He says 'it is permitted.' He thinks the whole prohibition does not exist.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he says 'It is permitted.'
phrases.notes: He thinks עבודה זרה itself is allowed. He does not just think one act is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּאוֹמֵר מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by giving a case that fits רבא too.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבא, no case of unknowing עבודה זרה can be found.
steps.terutzMaskana: One who thinks עבודה זרה is permitted is a case of unknowing עבודה זרה for everyone.

steps.title: Then רבא's unanswered question would be answered
steps.stepSummary: If 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' covers someone who thinks עבודה זרה is permitted, this answers רבא's question to רב נחמן. One who forgot both things brings only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then resolve the question רבא asked רב נחמן: if he forgot both this and that, what is the law? Resolve that he is liable for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the new case. It would answer a question that was famously left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 gave two שבת cases. רבא asked about a third: a person who forgot both that it is שבת and that the labors are forbidden. Thinking עבודה זרה is permitted is like forgetting both. Under the reading from step 16, that case gets only one חטאת, so רבא's open question would have an answer here.

keyTerms.meaning: Then resolve the question from here
He asked him a question
Forgetting both this and that: both שבת and that the labors are forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: This is not one of the two cases from step 13. It is a third case where he forgot both things. רבא's question about it had been left unanswered until now, and step 23 answers it.

phrases.english: Then resolve what he asked
רבא of רב נחמן:
if he forgot both this and that, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means he forgot it was שבת and also forgot the labors are forbidden.

phrases.english: Resolve that he is liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּפְשׁוֹט דִּבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'אומר מותר' case from step 21 by showing what it would lead to.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' as covering one who thinks עבודה זרה is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would answer רבא's question about העלם זה וזה, which was left unanswered. So the reading seems wrong.

steps.title: No problem, let it answer the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this is not a difficulty. We can indeed answer רבא's question from here.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult; resolve it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by accepting it. Yes, this does answer רבא's question, and that is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An open question is not a proof that no answer exists. The reading of 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' can stand, and it gives an answer: one who forgot both brings only one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult

steps.whatToRemember: The case of unknowing עבודה זרה is someone who thinks it is permitted. Reading the פסוק this way also answers רבא's question: one who forgot both שבת and the labors brings only one חטאת.

phrases.english: This is not difficult; and resolve it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, וְתִפְשׁוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 by accepting what it said would follow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Answering רבא's open question shows the reading is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is fine to answer רבא's question from here: one חטאת for העלם זה וזה.

steps.title: Can this verse even be about idol worship?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the whole attempt to apply 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' to עבודה זרה. That פסוק is in the chapter where each kind of sinner brings a different animal, but for עבודה זרה everyone brings a female goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can you really explain these verses as speaking about idol worship? Here, in this chapter, it says that an anointed priest brings a bull, a king brings a male goat, and a regular person brings a female lamb or a female goat. But about idol worship we learned: they agree that he brings a female goat, just like a regular person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the basic idea behind the last few steps: that the פסוק 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' is talking about עבודה זרה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק comes from ויקרא chapter 4, where the כהן גדול, the נשיא and the יחיד each bring a different קרבן. But a ברייתא says that for עבודה זרה even the כהן גדול brings a שעירה like a regular person. So עבודה זרה must follow a different chapter (במדבר 15), and this פסוק cannot be used for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The anointed priest, meaning the כהן גדול
The king or ruler
A regular individual person
A female goat
'And they agree', meaning everyone holds this

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying a כהן גדול never brings a bull. He does bring a bull for most sins. The point is that עבודה זרה is the exception, where he brings a female goat like everyone else.

phrases.english: But can you really set up
these verses as talking about idol worship?
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' (ויקרא 4:2) that the last few steps were built on.

phrases.english: For here it is written:
for the anointed priest, a bull;
for the king, a male goat;
and for an individual, a female lamb or a female goat.
Whereas about idol worship we learned:
And they agree that it is with a female goat, like an individual.
phrases.notes: Even a כהן גדול who served an idol by mistake brings the same female goat as anyone else.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לְהָנֵי קְרָאֵי בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 17-23 managed to find a workable case, this step undercuts the whole proposal of steps 15-16 to apply 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' to עבודה זרה at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' in ויקרא chapter 4 is talking about עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ויקרא chapter 4 gives different קרבנות for the כהן גדול, the נשיא and the יחיד, but for עבודה זרה all of them bring a שעירה. So עבודה זרה comes from a different chapter and cannot be learned from this פסוק.

steps.title: The attempt is closed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the discussion: the attempt to apply the פסוק to עבודה זרה fails, and the objection stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is nothing more to say.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this whole line of discussion with a short final phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is given to the challenge in step 24, so it stands. The search for an עבודה זרה case under 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' is dropped, and the original objection (רב יוסף's challenge to רבי אבא) remains in force.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And nothing more': the discussion is finished and the challenge stands

steps.whatToRemember: The laws of a mistaken עבודה זרה קרבן do not come from ויקרא chapter 4. That is why every attempt to use 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' for עבודה זרה fails.

phrases.english: And nothing more.
phrases.notes: Meaning: there is no answer, so the challenge wins and this line of thinking is dropped.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ לָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 24 as final.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'ועשה מאחת מהנה' cannot be applied to עבודה זרה, so the earlier objection stands.

steps.title: Introducing רב שמואל בר יהודה's statement
steps.stepSummary: A new section begins: רב שמואל בר יהודה arrived and said something. His actual words come right after this line.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב שמואל בר יהודה came, he said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It introduces a new teaching from רב שמואל בר יהודה, which continues right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is only the opening attribution line. The content of what he said follows next. The phrase 'כי אתא' usually means a sage came from ארץ ישראל to בבל and brought a teaching with him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When he came', usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing a teaching

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה, אָמַר:
phrases.english: When Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda came, he said:

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 25 closes the previous attempt, this line opens a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening attribution only; the content of the statement follows next.
